issues: whether the total delay from charge to trial violates the right to be tried within a reasonable time under s. 11(b) of the Charter
the framework for assessing whether criminal trial delay is unreasonable (Jordan v Canada and pre-Jordan factors)
the significance of delay attributable to the Crown, including scheduling and case-management delays
whether the delay is excusable or attributable to the accused
the remedy of a stay of proceedings for unreasonable delay in a criminal prosecution
the distinction between pre-charge and post-charge delay in the reasonableness analysis
key_facts: approximately three years elapsed from charge to trial
trial still ongoing in provincial court
much of the delay caused by Crown scheduling
causes_of_action: violation of the right to a trial within a reasonable time
candidate_statutes: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 11(b)
